questions.text: A company has computers in offices in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt. Which network type is needed to connect those geographically separated office networks?
opts: A single local-area network confined to one office
questions.explanation: A WAN connects networks over longer distances.

questions.text: Which device forwards packets between networks using destination IP addresses and routing information?
questions.explanation: Routers forward packets between networks.

questions.text: What is the main role of DNS in ordinary web browsing?
opts: Convert a domain name into an IP address
Encrypt every file on a computer
questions.explanation: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - AMS103_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Which technology primarily describes the structure and content of a webpage?
questions.explanation: HTML defines webpage structure and content.

questions.text: A program secretly records a user’s keystrokes and sends passwords to an attacker. This is most specifically a:
questions.explanation: A keylogger captures keystrokes, often to steal credentials.

questions.text: Which sequence best represents the main stages of analogue-to-digital conversion described in the assessment?
questions.explanation: The assessment describes sampling, quantisation and encoding.

questions.text: Why is binary suitable for digital computer hardware?
opts: Hardware switches can reliably represent two states
Binary prevents every possible software error
Binary eliminates the need for memory
questions.explanation: Two-state hardware makes binary representation reliable.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - AMS103_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives each ready process a fixed time slice before moving to the next?
questions.explanation: Round robin uses a time quantum for each process.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - AMS103_mock Section A (printed answer key)

questions.text: What happens during a page fault in a demand-paging system when the required page is not in physical memory?
opts: The operating system handles the missing page, typically loading it from storage
The router changes the destination IP address
The monitor converts sound into a digital signal
questions.explanation: The OS handles the absent page and may load it from storage.

questions.text: What is the main difference between DSL and optical fibre transmission?
opts: DSL uses copper telephone lines; optical fibre carries light through fibre strands
DSL uses light in glass; optical fibre uses copper electrical signals
Both require only wireless radio signals

Optical fibre cannot transmit digital information Section A answer key Q Answer Reason 1 B A WAN connects networks over longer distances. 2 A Routers forward packets between networks. 3 A DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses. 4 B HTML defines webpage structure and content. 5 A A keylogger captures keystrokes, often to steal credentials. 6 B The assessment describes sampling, quantisation and encoding. 7 A Two-state hardware makes binary representation reliable. 8 A Round robin uses a time quantum for each process. 9 A The OS handles the absent page and may load it from storage. 10 A
questions.explanation: DSL sends data as electrical signals over existing copper telephone lines, with speed falling over distance. Optical fibre sends pulses of LIGHT through glass strands, giving far higher bandwidth over longer distances with less interference.

questions.text: Which network normally connects devices across multiple cities?
questions.explanation: A WAN (Wide Area Network) links computers and LANs across cities, countries or continents using telecom infrastructure. A LAN covers a single site, like one office or campus.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which type of malware is designed to secretly collect user information?
questions.explanation: Spyware covertly monitors activity and transmits personal data (passwords, browsing, keystrokes). It neither encrypts files like ransomware nor spreads itself like a worm - its purpose is stealthy information gathering.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: What is the correct order for analogue-to-digital conversion in the assessment material?
questions.explanation: The assessment's order is: SAMPLING (measure the analogue signal at regular intervals), QUANTISATION (round each sample to the nearest digital level), then ENCODING (represent each level as binary numbers).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - mixed 12-Q test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: The key difference between a LAN and a WAN is:
opts: A LAN covers a limited area; a WAN connects networks over larger geographical distances
A LAN is always wireless; a WAN is always wired
A WAN is faster than a LAN in every case
They are two names for the same thing
questions.explanation: The course's key answer: LAN = limited area; WAN = larger geographical distances; organisations may use both.

questions.text: Which malware type self-propagates across networks without needing to attach to a file?
questions.explanation: The guide: a virus attaches to files, while a worm self-propagates.

questions.text: Malware that disguises itself as legitimate software is a:
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse disguises malicious software as legitimate.

questions.text: Ransomware typically:
opts: Encrypts data or blocks access and demands payment
questions.explanation: The guide: ransomware encrypts data or blocks access to demand payment.

questions.text: The correct order for analogue-to-digital conversion is:
questions.explanation: The assessment material orders ADC as sampling, then quantisation, then encoding.

questions.text: One second of mono audio sampled at 44,100 samples/second with 16 bits per sample requires approximately:
questions.explanation: 44,100 x 16 = 705,600 bits; divided by 8 = 88,200 bytes (~88.2 kB), per the course's worked calculation.

questions.text: Computers use binary representation because:
opts: Hardware circuits reliably distinguish two states (on/off)
Binary numbers are shorter to write
questions.explanation: Digital hardware is built on two-state devices, so binary (two states) is the natural representation.

questions.text: The primary purpose of a computer virus is:
opts: Replicating and spreading to other files
questions.explanation: A virus's defining behaviour is replicating itself and spreading to other files or programs.

questions.text: Which type of malware disguises itself as a legitimate program?
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse masquerades as useful or legitimate software to trick users into running it.

questions.text: The key characteristic of a worm is that it:
opts: Hides in the boot sector only
questions.explanation: Unlike viruses, worms self-propagate across networks without needing to attach to a host file.

questions.text: Malware that encrypts files and demands payment is:
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts the victim's data or blocks access and demands a ransom.

questions.text: The purpose of a rootkit is:
opts: Concealing unauthorised access to a system
questions.explanation: Rootkits hide the presence of unauthorised access or malicious software on an infected system.

questions.text: In a phishing attack, users are tricked into revealing sensitive information mainly by:
questions.explanation: Phishing impersonates a trusted party (bank, service, colleague) to obtain credentials or data.

questions.text: A DDoS attack is characterised by:
opts: Overloading a server with traffic from many sources
questions.explanation: A distributed denial-of-service attack floods a target with traffic from many compromised machines.
